title: Quantum Error Correction
summary: The 3-qubit bit-flip code, syndromes and the error threshold.
mission: Protect qubit 0 against bit flips: encode it into three qubits (encode), measure the syndrome on two ancillas without touching the state, and correct the affected qubit (recover). The logical state must survive an X on any of the three qubits, for any input state.

prediction.question: An X error hits qubits 0 and 1 at the same time. What does the code do?
options: Fails: the syndrome points to qubit 2, and the result becomes a logical X
Destroys the state, which becomes a mixture
prediction.explanation: Two flips on qubits 0 and 1 give the same syndrome as a single flip on qubit 2. The code applies X to qubit 2 and ends up with all three inverted: a logical error. It corrects one flip, not two.

hints: Encoding copies the basis, not the state: qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 1]) and qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 2]) take α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ to α|000⟩ + β|111⟩.
Syndrome: ancilla 3 stores the parity of qubits 0 and 1 (CNOT from 0 and from 1 to 3); ancilla 4, that of qubits 1 and 2. Each single flip gives a different pair of bits: X0 → 10, X1 → 11, X2 → 01.
Correction without measuring: qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 4, target]) acts when both ancillas are 1. For the pattern 10, wrap it with qml.PauliX on the ancilla that must be 0 (before and after).
